data.title: WaFd outlines EverBank deal economics with 29% EPS accretion target and first calendar quarter 2027 close timeline
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: WaFd (WAFD) Q4 2026

Management view

  • “We closed out our fiscal year 2026 on a high note with earnings per share up 22% over the prior year.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall)

  • “In what is likely to be our final fiscal year before we merge with EverBank, we are proud to deliver our second best year ever in terms of after-tax net income of $241 million.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “WaFd Inc. reported net income available to common shareholders of $56.3 million or $0.76 per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.” (Executive VP & CFO Kelli Holz)

  • “The company sold $543 million of single-family residential loans during the quarter and has entered into an agreement to sell $429 million of multifamily loans in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Absent any changes in interest rates, we expect our margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or 2 with the reduction in earning assets due to the loan sales in addition to our earning assets repricing more quickly than our liabilities in the short term in a rising rate environment.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Ultimately, this relationship resulted in a large impairment well outside of our historical loss results.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Ryan Mauer)

  • “Our previously announced expected closing time frame of the first calendar quarter 2027 remains on track.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “With all of that for context, the question I receive most often now is why did WaFd decide to partner with EverBank?” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “Our pro forma bank… shows that with a 3% margin… we can achieve just shy of a 15% return on tangible common equity.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “Through this merger, we will be able to fair value the WaFd balance sheet, including the $6.6 billion of single-family residential loans that are today earning only 4.25% and mark those loans to market rates.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “We were able to do it with the following metrics: 9.8% pro forma CET1 at close, only 8% dilution to WaFd existing shareholders and 29% EPS accretion to WaFd shareholders once the cost saves are fully realized.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

Outlook

  • No analyst-estimate comparison was included because the provided estimates tag did not contain a valid fiscalQuarter format.

  • “Absent any changes in interest rates, we expect our margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or 2.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Earlier this month, we filed our regulatory applications, and we expect to file our proxy within the next 2 weeks.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “Our previously announced expected closing time frame of the first calendar quarter 2027 remains on track.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

Financial results

  • No analyst-estimate comparison was included because the provided estimates tag did not contain a valid fiscalQuarter format.

  • “WaFd Inc. reported net income available to common shareholders of $56.3 million or $0.76 per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026… and $0.84 per share for the June 2026 quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Loans receivable decreased $977 million during the quarter as a result of the loan sale-related activity.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “We expect to realize a net gain of approximately $7 million when this sale is finalized.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Total deposits increased by $389 million during the quarter… Core deposits ended the quarter at 81.8% compared to the June quarter at 80.6% of total deposits.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “The net interest margin held steady at 2.81%, no change from the June 30, 2026 quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Total noninterest income was $38.1 million for the September 2026 quarter compared to $24.2 million for the prior quarter… primarily driven by a $16.4 million gain on the sale of single-family loans during the quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Total noninterest expense was $121.5 million compared to $110.3 million for the June quarter… combined with $6.2 million in merger-related costs incurred in the fourth quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “$39.2 million of net charge-offs were taken during the quarter, inclusive of the problem loan mentioned previously.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Mauer)

Q&A

  • Jeff Rulis, D.A. Davidson & Co., Research Division: “Maybe if I could hop into the loan sales. What timing of that in the quarter… and then the average yield on those buckets of the sale?” Executive VP & CFO Holz: “We closed on the single-family sale towards the end of September… and we signed our purchase and sale agreement on the multifamily sale actually on the last day of the quarter… The single-family is reflective of a rate in the 4.25%, 4.30%, 4.40% range… and… multifamily… is in about 4.8% today.”

  • Jeff Rulis, D.A. Davidson & Co., Research Division: “Was there a selection process… And… any more coming…?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “Obviously, these came from the Luther Burbank portfolio… So that gave us the opportunity for the gain… we don't have immediate plans… but we'll continue to be opportunistic.”

  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: “Loans are going to be down roughly $1 billion with the multifamily loan sale… do you anticipate any offset…?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “We haven't made definitive plans, nothing to announce… we're expecting our margin to go up, and we'll work to defend the NII.”

  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: “Just on the expense run rate this quarter… thoughts on that run rate going forward?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “Typically, this quarter is a little bit hotter… I think we'll probably be there to a little bit flat on the next quarter.”

  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: “What's the beta you're assuming on interest-bearing deposits…?” Executive VP & CFO Holz: “I think about 50%.”

  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: “Is there any appetite to buy back shares…?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “There's certainly appetite, but given where we're at with the proxy… we're not in a position to be buying back shares today.”

  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens Inc., Research Division: “Should we expect expenses moderate from here? Or is $115 million kind of the true run rate…?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “I think that number is a fair number to use in your models.”

  • Kelly Motta, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division: “Just wondering how those conversations are going?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “I'd say the meetings are characterized with optimism… Sincerely, I am more excited about the deal today than when we announced it a month ago.”

  • Kelly Motta, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division: “How much is going to be used to pay down borrowings versus reinvestment…?” President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall: “We haven't made those final determinations yet… but… we will work to defend our NII number… we're not looking to shrink our income.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to pressing on near-term profitability mechanics around loan-sale-driven earning asset declines and expense run-rate, including “Loans are going to be down roughly $1 billion” (Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division) and “as we think about… how much is going to be used to pay down borrowings versus reinvestment” (Kelly Motta, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division).

  • Management tone in prepared remarks was positive and strategic on the EverBank rationale and pro forma targets, including “this is a game changer” and “29% EPS accretion” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall), while Q&A responses were more guarded on near-term actions, including “we haven't made definitive plans, nothing to announce” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall).

  • Versus the prior quarter, prepared-remark tone shifted from highlighting share-price strength (“we were pleased to see the stock provide a 23% total shareholder return for the quarter”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q3) to acknowledging market pushback on the announced deal (“Since we announced our deal, our stock is down 18.9%… roughly a 10% delta.”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q4).

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance language on margin shifted from “we expect our margin to be relatively flat for the next quarter” (Executive VP & CFO Kelli Holz, Q3) to “we expect our margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or 2” (Executive VP & CFO Holz, Q4).

  • Credit narrative shifted from a pending resolution to a realized loss: “Outstanding balances for this relationship amounts to $54 million… with anticipated sale of the business” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Ryan Mauer, Q3) versus “this relationship resulted in a large impairment” and “$39.2 million of net charge-offs” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Mauer, Q4).

  • Capital and buyback discussion moved from flexibility (“We will continue to be opportunistic with our share repurchases”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall, Q3) to constraint (“we're not in a position to be buying back shares today”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q4).

  • Strategy emphasis broadened from Build 2030 execution and organic loan/deposit growth (Q3) to a merger-led business model shift: “we are changing our business model so that we are not solely reliant on noninterest-bearing deposit growth to hit our return goals” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q4).

Risks and concerns

  • “This loss was significant for the bank and is well outside of our normalized loss history.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Ryan Mauer)

  • “The economic uncertainty driven by continued inflationary pressures, energy supply shocks driven by the war in the Middle East and tariffs will continue to impact the borrowers' top line revenue results as well as operating costs.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Mauer)

  • “All of this is, of course, pending receipt of the requisite approvals from both shareholders and regulators.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall)

  • “You cannot argue with the market.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

Final takeaway

Management framed Q4 as a quarter with steady margin, higher noninterest income from loan sales, and elevated credit costs tied to a single large C&I impairment, while emphasizing merger economics and timing for the EverBank transaction, including a first calendar quarter 2027 close expectation and pro forma targets such as “29% EPS accretion” and “just shy of a 15% return on tangible common equity” under a “3% margin” scenario.

data.title: AES wins European Union approval for sale to GIM and EQT Fund Management
data.description:
AES Corp. (AES) won approval from the European Union's antitrust regulator for its planned $15 a share sale to Global Infrastructure Management and EQT Infrastructure. 

The European Commission concluded that the deal wouldn't raise competition concerns, given the companies' limited market positions resulting from the proposed transaction, according to a  statement on the regulator's website on Friday.

Last month, AES Corp. (AES) disclosed that it received approval from the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio  for its planned sale to a consortium led by BlackRock's (BLK) Global Infrastructure and EQT Infrastructure.  AES (AES) in August said it won approval from the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States for the combination.

AES in March agreed to be acquired by a consortium led by GIM and EQT,  along with co-underwriters California Public Employees Retirement System and Qatar Investment Authority, for $15/share in cash, representing a total equity value of $10.7B and an enterprise value of ~$33.4B including debt.

data.title: Cohen & Steers signals continued operating leverage with compensation at ~40% of revenues as pipeline stands at $1.9B
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Cohen & Steers (CNS) Q3 2026

Management view

  • Cohen & Steers reported accelerating organic growth alongside softer ending AUM due to markets. Chief Financial Officer Amit Muni said, “We generated $1.6 billion of net inflows, representing our fifth consecutive quarter of organic growth and our strongest flow period since the fourth quarter of 2021,” while adding, “We ended the quarter with assets under management of $95.9 billion, down from $100 billion last quarter as negative market movement offset the strong flows generated during the period.”

  • Management highlighted broader participation across channels and strategies. CFO Muni said, “At the strategy level, every investment strategy generated positive net inflows led by real estate, multi-strategy real assets and preferred securities,” and noted, “Our institutional pipeline also increased to $1.9 billion from $1.6 billion last quarter.”

  • CEO Joseph Harvey emphasized wealth-led growth and ETF expansion, saying, “Our wealth channel continues to drive organic growth with $1.3 billion of net inflows this quarter,” and “Adoption of our active ETFs is accelerating with growth of 22% during the quarter to $1.3 billion.” Harvey also announced a product launch: “We launched our seventh active ETF in August, the Cohen & Steers Real Assets Active ETF, symbol CSRA.”

  • Management flagged near-term institutional outflows not tied to performance. CEO Harvey said, “Looking ahead, we have been notified of approximately $400 million in partial account rebalancing outflows from 2 institutional clients, which are not related to investment performance.”

  • The company disclosed a senior hire in marketing. CEO Harvey said, “We are pleased to welcome Erik Schneberger to Cohen & Steers as our new Chief Marketing Officer.”

  • President and Chief Investment Officer John Cheigh pointed to a rebound in quarterly investment outcomes, stating, “74% of our AUM outperformed in the third quarter, up from 40% in the second quarter,” and adding, “we believe our REIT performance is back on trend.”

Outlook

  • The company did not issue EPS or revenue guidance for the next quarter or full year in this transcript; management instead reiterated expense framework and discussed flows/pipeline expectations.

  • CFO Muni said, “Looking ahead, we are maintaining our expense guidance,” specifying, “We continue to expect compensation and benefits expenses of approximately 40% of revenues, mid-single-digit growth in G&A expenses relative to 2025 and a pro forma effective tax rate of 25% to 26%.”

  • On visibility into growth, CEO Harvey pointed to pipeline replenishment and funding pace: “Our won and unfunded pipeline grew to $1.9 billion in the third quarter, the second-largest ever,” and “the velocity of the pipeline continues with $700 million of fundings reloaded with over $1.1 billion of new mandates awarded within the quarter.”

Financial results

  • CFO Muni reported, “We reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.89, up from $0.85 in the second quarter,” and added, “Net income was $46.5 million for the quarter.”

  • Revenue and expenses moved higher on average AUM and incentive compensation accruals. CFO Muni said, “Revenues increased 3% to $156 million,” and “Total operating expenses increased 2% to $98 million.”

  • Profitability improved sequentially, with CFO Muni stating, “Our operating margin expanded to 37.2%, reflecting the benefit of higher revenues and controlled expenses.”

Q&A

  • John Dunn, Evercore ISI Institutional Equities, Research Division asked about sustaining real estate demand with higher rates and differences across channels; President & Chief Investment Officer Cheigh answered, “we haven't really seen any kind of notable change in tone,” while CEO Harvey said, “our average daily flows increased in each of those months… no real impact on flow activity from the changes in the macro environment recently.”

  • John Dunn, Evercore ISI Institutional Equities, Research Division asked for more detail on SICAV demand and differences vs. the U.S.; CEO Harvey responded, “we've had a really strong quarter in flows… We’re at about $2.1 billion in overall AUM,” and said the firm is “seeing good activity in the U.K… South Africa, and… increasing activity in Asia.”

  • Ivory Gao, BofA Securities, Research Division asked if allocators are shifting from private to listed infrastructure due to liquidity and whether a semi-liquid product is being considered; CEO Harvey said interest is “not coming at the expense of private infrastructure,” and added, “We have something that's in the lab, but we're not ready to talk about it.”

  • Ivory Gao, BofA Securities, Research Division asked about AI/data center exposure across REIT and infrastructure strategies; President & Chief Investment Officer Cheigh said, “data centers are about 10% of our portfolio” in U.S. real estate, and in infrastructure “roughly 1/3… is in the utility space,” framing AI as “a big, but definitely not the only part” of power investment.

  • John Dunn, Evercore ISI Institutional Equities, Research Division asked about accelerating growth in CNSREIT and pipeline conversion timing/composition; CEO Harvey said CNSREIT is “the #1 performing nontraded REIT,” described scale as “about $900 million in total assets with equity value of about $400 million,” and added, “the life cycle in terms of getting to… from the pipeline to fund is roughly about 4 months.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical, with repeated questions centered on higher-rate sensitivity, durability of real estate demand, and how much growth depends on AI/data centers.

  • Management’s tone was slightly positive and explanatory in prepared remarks, leaning on breadth of inflows and pipeline, and in Q&A emphasized steadiness of demand; Cheigh said, “we haven't really seen any kind of notable change in tone,” while Harvey stressed, “no real impact on flow activity.”

  • Versus last quarter, management commentary shifted from a “resilient global economy” backdrop in Q2 to acknowledging that “sharp rise in long-term treasury yields now above 5%” created “near-term pressure” in Q3, while maintaining confidence in valuation/fundamentals.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Flows and pipeline strengthened sequentially, with Q3 net inflows of $1.6 billion vs. $1.3 billion in Q2 and the institutional pipeline at $1.9 billion vs. $1.6 billion.

  • Ending AUM declined to $95.9 billion in Q3 from “over $100 billion” in Q2, as Q3 management cited “negative market movement” versus Q2’s “positive market performance.”

  • Investment performance messaging improved, with Cheigh citing Q3 quarterly outperformance breadth rising to 74% vs. 40% in Q2; Q2 discussion had centered on a “1-year outlier” driven by U.S. REIT positioning.

  • Strategic emphasis continued on ETFs and international distribution; Q3 added the CSRA launch and a new Chief Marketing Officer, while Q2 included distribution operating changes and detailed ETF platforming/launch cadence.

Risks and concerns

  • Rate-driven valuation pressure remained a key macro risk; President & Chief Investment Officer Cheigh said, “Higher interest rates have weighed on our asset classes,” and pointed to “long-term treasury yields now above 5%.”

  • Institutional flows were described as uneven, and management flagged specific upcoming outflows; CEO Harvey said the approximately $400 million in rebalancing outflows were “not related to investment performance,” and pointed to pipeline replenishment as support.

  • Management framed AI-related exposure as present but limited in direct portfolio concentration; Cheigh said data centers are “about 10%” of U.S. real estate and infrastructure exposure is largely indirect through utilities.

Final takeaway

Management described Q3 as a quarter of broadening growth with $1.6 billion of net inflows, improving investment performance breadth, and a larger $1.9 billion institutional pipeline, while acknowledging that rising long-term yields pressured markets and reduced ending AUM. Executives reiterated expense expectations—compensation and benefits at approximately 40% of revenues, mid-single-digit G&A growth vs. 2025, and a 25% to 26% pro forma tax rate—while pointing to accelerating active ETF adoption, the August launch of CSRA, and continued international and institutional expansion as key drivers entering the next period.

data.title: Wall Street fear gauge VIX surges to over four-month high
data.description:
The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) surged roughly 30% on Friday afternoon to trade above 21—reaching an over four-month high—amid circulating market rumors that a major hedge fund had collapsed.

After hovering near 16 throughout the morning session, the volatility gauge broke out sharply after midday, rising to an intraday high of 22.31 from a low of 15.73 before stabilizing near 21.43 at press time. The sudden afternoon spike marked a sharp departure from an otherwise quiet VIX action.

Market commentators pointed to institutional distress as a potential catalyst for the volatility spike. CNBC options reporter Oliver Renick noted that trading conditions shifted dramatically within a 30-minute window as rumors circulated that a market participant was "getting blown out."

Jim Cramer echoed concerns over forced liquidations, observing that pressure in energy markets alongside "a big hedge fund blowing up" made Friday one of the worst trading days of the year.

Wall Street’s major market averages were markedly lower Friday, with the S&P 500 Index (SP500) down 1.2%, as technology stocks came under further pressure and oil prices extended gains. WTI crude (CL1:COM) climbed above $100 per barrel, bringing its five-day increase to about 11%.

data.title: Martin Marietta raised to Buy at D.A. Davidson after YTD underperformance
data.description:
Martin Marietta Materials (MLM) climbed 1.1% in Friday's trading as D.A. Davidson upgraded the building materials company to Buy from Neutral with a $610 price target, saying the Lhoist North American acquisition lowers revenue and margin cyclicality, helping support valuation after theshares have underperformed YTD.

D.A. Davidson analyst Garik Shmois said he sees an attractive entry point for investors ahead of Q3 earnings and anticipated guidance for at least mid-single-digit to high-single-digit pricing in FY 2027, with upside potential as recent mix headwinds from NFS and Quikrete roll off.

High mid-single-digit to high-single-digit pricing should help price-cost spreads return to normal levels, assuming diesel prices remain flat and the company continues to execute on its plant automation and network optimization program, the analyst said.

Shmois also praised the combination with Lhoist North America that makes Martin Marietta (MLM) the top U.S. producer of limestone products, saying it provides greater end-market diversity, optionality to capture value from construction aggregates currently sold by third parties at LNA sites, and a more stable margin profile through energy hedges.

data.title: Alkermes reinstated Buy at Truist on narcolepsy opportunity
data.description:
Truist Securities on Friday reinstated its coverage of Alkermes (ALKS) with a Buy recommendation and a $55 per share target, citing the potential of its lead orexin development candidate, alixorexton, against narcolepsy, a sleeping disorder.

Analyst Alex Nackenoff argued that alixorexton has already shown a superior clinical profile against narcolepsy type 1, and its existing data is sufficiently strong in narcolepsy type 2 compared with oxybates.

However, according to Nackenoff, its proof-of-concept data expected from a Phase 2 trial for another neurological sleep disorder known as idiopathic hypersomnia represents the key near-term catalyst for the stock.

“The readout expected toward the end of 2026 presents an attractive risk/reward opportunity; we believe positive data could translate to potentially +20% on the upside with minimal downside risk if negative,” he added.

While Takeda (TAK) is set to launch the first OX2R product branded as Orzeyful later this year, its opportunity is limited to NT1, according to Nackenoff. "Alixorexton has already demonstrated better efficacy vs. Orzeyful in NT1, and we feel the data is sufficiently strong in NT2 to deliver significant clinical benefit over oxybates,” the analyst added.

data.title: Ambarella may be seeing interest from a third bidder - report
data.description:
Ambarella (AMBA) is speculated to have garnered interest from a third bidder. 

There's speculation that one of the world's biggest AI chipmakers has entered a sales process for Ambarella (AMBA), according to traders who cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert that was circulating on Friday. 

The bidding war now consists of the unidentified chipmaker, NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), and Qualcomm (QCOM). Betaville last Friday said Qualcomm (QCOM) is speculated to be working with banks on a potential deal. The third bidder is described as bigger than NXPI and QCOM combined.

There's some speculation that the sales process is in its late stages and a deal could be announced in the coming weeks, according to Betaville.

Betaville first reported about Ambarella (AMBA) takeover speculation in late July. Ambarella jumped 16% on July 31 following the FT report that NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) was in talks to acquire the chip designer.

Shares of Ambarella pared much of an earlier decline on Friday.

data.title: Victoria's Secret is still in the early innings of a multi-year turnaround - Needham
data.description:
Needham started off coverage on Victoria's Secret (VSXY) with a Buy rating on its view that the retailer is only in the early innings of a multi-year turnaround.

Analyst Tom Nikic pointed to improvements to the Victoria's Secret (VSXY) management team, product assortment, and the marketing upside. Notably, Nikic and his team think the VSXY's EPS can double over the next five  years. 

As for the near term, strong quarter-to-date channel checks and lower promotions have Nikic calling Victoria's Secret (VSXY) a compelling beat-and-raise story.

Looking ahead, the company is seen as being a beneficiary of increased adoption of GLP-1 weight loss medicines as slimmed-down women shop for new clothes. All in, we view this as a compelling momentum name heading into 2027

Needham assigned a price target of $106 on VSXY based on a 16X multiple to its FY28 EPS estimate. The PT assumes mid-single-digit revenue growth the next two years and EBIT margin expansion. 

Shares of VSXY are up more than 60% on a year-to-date basis, but the Seeking Alpha Quant Rating is still flashing Strong Buy.

data.title: Nasdaq plunges 2% and these 15 names have led the downward decline
data.description:
Technology stocks came under broad pressure Friday afternoon as investors rotated away from growth-oriented names and the wider tech sector.

The broader tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) and the more concentrated Nasdaq 100 Index (NDX) both fell more than 2% during the session. The Nasdaq Composite declined a total of 2.1%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.4%. The move reflected a clear risk-off tone concentrated in higher-valuation technology and growth companies.

Selling was widespread within the Nasdaq 100, where 73 of the index’s 100 constituents traded lower. CoreWeave (CRWV) led the declines, with the firm’s shares falling 12.6% and posting the steepest loss among index members.

data.title: Katie Zacharia has been ousted from her role as press secretary – report
data.description:
Current White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia has been ousted, according to three people familiar with the matter, New York Times reported Friday.

Zacharia has been under scrutiny due to how she presented her legal career and how she handled her press briefing. Her role as White House press secretary began on Oct. 12 and has reportedly lasted until Oct. 16.

President Donald Trump was questioned by reporters outside the White House and said, “Maybe the role is not for her.” He mentioned that he told her she did not have to stay in her role.

“I’m going to let her make the decision,” he said. “If I were her, I’d reconsider.”

Zacharia preceded Karoline Leavitt, who served the White House from January 2025 to August 2026.

The White House didn't immediately respond to Seeking Alpha’s request for comment.
